Key Activities: Develops and conducts research and modeling studies and writes/edits analytical material for publication purposes.
Provides advice and consultative services to data suppliers and users, and directs staff on the uses and preparation of estimates.
Provides feedback and recommendations for improvement on established statistical programs.
Leads project teams involved in the conduct of analytical research and modeling studies.
Represents the division as an analytical research and modeling specialist in the area of expertise on development projects, task forces and committees.

1. Decision making: Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines data sources, modifies existing methods and approaches for analytical research and modeling studies or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Develops guidelines, proposals and recommendations for divisional management to improve existing surveys or to initiate new surveys / projects.

Selects and evaluates analytical techniques and quantitative analytical methods to be used to integrate and interpret mass volumes of data. Projects may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and efforts must be made to translate them into common concepts.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit involved in statistical activities and/or leads multi-disciplinary project teams for special projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going analytical projects and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Procures goods and services according to approved budget allocations.
3. Communication: Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics). When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex data, reasons for variances in the results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of statistical and analytical methods and approaches used. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of surveys or projects, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.

Provides expertise, advice and interpretation to decision-makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This often requires the adaptation and presentation of complex information in basic, understandable formats. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and workgroups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices in order to plan and implement analytical research and modeling studies and to recommend and implement improvements to statistical programs.

Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory especially as they relate to a specialized area (e.g. System of National Accounts, Health, Justice, Education, Labor, Prices, Demography, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). This is necessary to conduct analytical research and modeling studies and to assess the content of articles and reports that will be distributed widely or published.
Knowledge of the theories and principles of management to lead a multi-disciplinary unit or project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of analytical projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage analytical projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.
Knowledge of the policies and programs, of key client departments, to determine their information requirements and identify analysis opportunities.

Knowledge of data users and suppliers from all levels of government, and the private sector to discuss data reporting agreements; to understand their needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide them with expert advice on study or survey results.

Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to the area of expertise in a statistical program (e.g. System of National Accounts, Education, Health, Labor, Prices, Demography, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). This knowledge is required to analyze and interpret the data and assess their impact on the area of specialization. International public and private organizations involved in the area of statistics or in the area of expertise. This is necessary to share information.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request. Determines data requirements and sources, and recommends modifications to the content and coverage of studies, procedures, concepts, methods and definitions.

Writes analytical papers and articles on the interpretation of surveys, statistical applications or project findings, their application to the area of specialization and the methodology used. This information is published and used by specialized groups of interest (e.g. academics, private sector industries , etc.) and Federal and provincial departments for decision / policy making purposes.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures; reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs; conceptualizes enhancements or proposes modifications to study and/or program content and coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied. Each project is unique in nature and may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources.

Selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data. Reviews and modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Often, these data come from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) and have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts. There is a requirement to integrate data from diverse sources and concepts into a common conceptual framework and to identify and measure complex and subtle relationships among variables to produce statistical information.

Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Education: Degree with Economics Sociology or Statistics Specialization
Experience: Knowledge Translation and Storytelling Through Presentations or Publications
Providing Advice and Producing Briefing Materials
Competencies: Showing Initiative and Being Action Oriented
